comparisons.peer_topic: Impact of Pillar Two on company's 2024 financials
comparisons.peer_summary: The impact of Pillar Two legislation on the company for the fiscal year 2024 was immaterial, and the company continues to evaluate the impact of proposed and enacted legislative changes on its effective tax rate and cash flows as new guidance becomes available.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies address the impact of OECD Pillar Two legislation on their effective tax rates. Intels disclosure broadly lists changes in tax laws including Pillar Two as a factor causing significant variability in financial results. In contrast, AMD specifically states that the impact of Pillar Two for fiscal year 2024 was immaterial, though it continues to evaluate ongoing legislative changes.

sentences.text: ▪changes in US federal, state, or foreign tax laws or their interpretation, including the global implementation of a minimum tax under Pillar Two of the OECD BEPS initiative;
For 2024, the impact to us associated with Pillar Two was immaterial.
We continue to evaluate the impact of proposed and enacted legislative changes to our effective tax rate and cash flows as new guidance becomes available.

comparisons.peer_summary: Estimates and judgments are required for calculating tax liabilities and determining the recoverability of deferred tax assets arising from temporary differences between tax and financial reporting.
comparisons.comparison: Intels disclosure highlights changes in the valuation of deferred tax assets and liabilities as a key factor impacting the effective tax rate. AMD similarly identifies that determining the recoverability of deferred tax assets requires significant estimates and judgments, linking this to the same underlying accounting complexity regarding deferred tax valuations.

sentences.text: ▪changes in the valuation of our deferred tax assets and liabilities, and in deferred tax valuation allowances;

These estimates and judgments are applied in the calculation of certain tax liabilities and in the determination of the recoverability of deferred tax assets which arise from temporary differences between the recognition of assets and liabilities for tax and financial statement reporting purposes.

comparisons.peer_summary: Significant management judgment is required to determine income tax provisions, deferred tax assets/liabilities, and valuation allowances, considering future taxable income and tax planning strategies.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies identify the assessment of deferred tax assets and valuation allowances as a critical area requiring significant management judgment. Intels disclosure notes that changes in the valuation of deferred tax assets and liabilities impact the effective tax rate, while AVGO states that significant management judgment is required to determine these items and any necessary valuation allowances.

sentences.text: ▪changes in the valuation of our deferred tax assets and liabilities, and in deferred tax valuation allowances;

Significant management judgment is required in developing our provision for or benefit from income taxes, including the determination of deferred tax assets and liabilities and any valuation allowances that might be required against the deferred tax assets.

comparisons.peer_topic: OECD Pillar Two Tax Legislation Impact
comparisons.peer_summary: The OECD Pillar Two legislation is effective for the company in 2025 and is expected not to materially impact the 2025 effective tax rate. However, other countries including Singapore plan to adopt similar legislation effective in 2026, which would significantly increase tax expense.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies discuss the implications of OECD Pillar Two legislation. Intels disclosure lists changes in tax laws, including Pillar Two, as a source of variability in the effective tax rate. MU provides a forward-looking perspective, noting that while Pillar Two is expected to be immaterial for 2025, future enactments in jurisdictions like Singapore could significantly increase tax expense.

sentences.text: ▪changes in US federal, state, or foreign tax laws or their interpretation, including the global implementation of a minimum tax under Pillar Two of the OECD BEPS initiative;

While we do not expect these enacted laws to materially impact our effective tax rate for 2025, additional countries where we operate, including Singapore, have announced plans to adopt Pillar Two legislation.
Enactment of this legislation would become effective for us in 2026 and significantly increase our tax expense.

comparisons.peer_topic: OECD Pillar Two Global Minimum Tax Impact
comparisons.peer_summary: While Pillar Two legislation has been enacted in certain jurisdictions starting in fiscal year 2025, it is not expected to materially impact NVIDIA's effective tax rate or cash flows in the next fiscal year based on current enacted laws, though new legislation could change this assessment.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies address the impact of OECD Pillar Two legislation on their financial results. Intels disclosure identifies changes in tax laws including Pillar Two as a factor causing significant variability in the effective tax rate. NVDA similarly evaluates the impact of Pillar Two but explicitly states that based on enacted laws, it is not expected to materially impact the effective tax rate or cash flows in the next fiscal year.

sentences.text: ▪changes in US federal, state, or foreign tax laws or their interpretation, including the global implementation of a minimum tax under Pillar Two of the OECD BEPS initiative;

The OECD, and its member countries, continue to release new guidance and legislation on Pillar Two and we continue to evaluate the impact on our financial position of the global implementation of these rules.
Based on enacted laws, Pillar Two is not expected to materially impact our effective tax rate or cash flows in the next fiscal year.

comparisons.peer_topic: Income Tax Jurisdictions and Deferred Tax Estimation
comparisons.peer_summary: The company is subject to income taxes in the U.S. and foreign jurisdictions, with deferred tax assets and liabilities based on estimates and judgments involving complex tax law uncertainties that may change due to new certainty, regulatory changes, or other circumstances.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies discuss the complexity of calculating deferred taxes and the reliance on estimates. Intels disclosure cites changes in the valuation of deferred tax assets and liabilities as a driver of effective tax rate variability. NVDA states that its calculation of deferred tax assets and liabilities involves estimates and judgments dealing with uncertainties in complex tax laws, which may change due to regulatory changes.

sentences.text: ▪changes in the valuation of our deferred tax assets and liabilities, and in deferred tax valuation allowances;
Our calculation of deferred tax assets and liabilities is based on certain estimates and judgments and involves dealing with uncertainties in the application of complex tax laws.

Our estimates of deferred tax assets and liabilities may change based, in part, on added certainty or finality to an anticipated outcome, changes in accounting standards or tax laws in the U.S. or foreign jurisdictions where we operate, or changes in other facts or circumstances.

comparisons.peer_topic: OECD Pillar Two Global Minimum Tax Impact
comparisons.peer_summary: The OECD announced a framework for a 15% global minimum tax (Pillar Two), with legislation in certain countries set to apply to the company starting in fiscal year 2025. QCOM does not currently expect a material impact on consolidated financial statements but continues to monitor implementation and OECD guidance.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies discuss the status of OECD Pillar Two legislation. Intels disclosure lists changes in tax laws, including Pillar Two, as a factor impacting the effective tax rate. QCOM notes that while Pillar Two legislation applies beginning in fiscal year 2025, it does not currently expect a material impact on its consolidated financial statements.

sentences.text: ▪changes in US federal, state, or foreign tax laws or their interpretation, including the global implementation of a minimum tax under Pillar Two of the OECD BEPS initiative;
Certain countries have implemented or are in the process of implementing the Pillar Two legislation, which will apply to us beginning in fiscal year 2025.

While we do not currently expect this to materially impact our consolidated financial statements, we continue to monitor the impact as countries implement legislation and the OECD provides additional guidance.
